s1.syndrome_frame: A subacute to chronic calvarial lesion with recent increase in size and pain
salient_findings: Hyperostotic lesion of the outer table of the right calvarium
Densely calcified mass involving the inferior squamosal portion of the right temporal bone
Low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images with mild patchy internal enhancement
key_facts: 28-year-old man with a history of migraine disorder
Several months of pain and swelling in the right mastoid area
Recent subjective enlargement of the mass and increased pain
Noncontrast CT showed a 3.0 × 3.0 × 1.1 cm hyperostotic lesion
MRI revealed a densely calcified mass measuring 3.6 × 1.5 × 3.0 cm
No intracranial extension or adjacent soft-tissue mass
Thickening of the inner table and a small amount of fluid in the right mastoid air cells
Mucosal thickening present in the right ethmoid air cells
Laboratory studies, including CBC, BMP, TSH, and free T4, were within normal limits

shortlist.label: Osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign appearance on initial imaging and densely calcified mass on MRI

shortlist.label: Osteochondroma
shortlist.why_kept: Considered as part of the surface bone and recent increase in size and pain

shortlist.label: Fibrous Dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of hyperostotic lesion and calvarial involvement

shortlist.label: Calvarial Fibrous Dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Specific type of fibrous dysplasia affecting the calvarium

shortlist.label: Ossifying Fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign fibro-osseous lesion that can cause calvarial lesions

raw.rationale: The presence of a densely calcified mass with low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images and mild patchy internal enhancement, along with the hyperostotic lesion on noncontrast CT, is most consistent with an osteoma, which is a benign bone tumor that can cause localized pain and swelling.

rejected.label: Osteochondroma
rejected.why: Osteochondroma typically presents with a cartilaginous cap and is less likely to be densely calcified.

rejected.label: Fibrous Dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia often has a ground-glass appearance on imaging and may have a more complex clinical presentation.

rejected.label: Calvarial Fibrous Dysplasia
rejected.why: Similar to fibrous dysplasia, calvarial fibrous dysplasia would likely have a distinct ground-glass appearance and possibly more extensive involvement.

rejected.label: Ossifying Fibroma
rejected.why: Ossifying fibroma can have a more aggressive appearance on imaging and may have a softer tissue component, which is not seen in this case.
